scenario: A full-time writer and coder is considering the roughly fifty-dollar Royal Kludge RK71 because its seller page presents a compact wireless mechanical keyboard with a 75-percent aggregate score across 12 reviews. The investigation requires four distinct checks: audit what the listing actually promises, interpret two independently discoverable same-model hobbyist reports without turning anecdotes into prevalence, explain what general contact-bounce mechanics can and cannot diagnose, and define a return-window test plan before treating the keyboard as suitable for daily work.
target: Audit the exact RK71 offer and its conflicting backlight language, distinguish the concrete layout and software-detection risks in two same-model hobbyist reports from any model-wide failure claim, explain contact bounce while preserving the boundary between a general mechanism and an RK71 diagnosis, and make a conditional purchase judgment with a reproducible pre-keep test and return protocol. State explicitly that the evidence does not establish months-later RK71 chatter frequency, lifespan, repairability, or warranty quality.
